statement: enforcer_rules::registry::RuleRecord has no status/Proposed field yet (out of d08's owns: scope, owned by d01/arc-14's enforcer-rules crate). d08 models the PROPOSED status as a d08-local wrapper (feedback::ProposedRule{status: feedback::RuleStatus, scaffold: ScaffoldOutput}) rather than editing the shared registry DTO. RuleStatus is a closed enum (only Proposed today) so a future Promoted/Rejected variant is non-breaking, matching the workpack's 'a Tier/status field, not prose' requirement.
why: Editing enforcer-rules::registry::RuleRecord would collide with d01/arc-14 file ownership and there is no scan-engine consumer of a status field yet (enforcer-scan does not reference RuleRecord/RuleRegistry at all on this branch) to actually wire a skip-if-Proposed behavior into. Keeping ProposedRule a DISTINCT type from RuleRecord proves 'non-blocking in a scan' at this module's own boundary without needing that consumer: nothing in enforcer-mechanization's own output can reach a live RuleRegistry without an explicit, separate promotion step.
howToApply: A future pack that adds a real status field to RuleRecord (or a scan-engine PROPOSED-skip) should fold feedback::RuleStatus into that shared enum rather than inventing a second one; feedback::ProposedRule::scaffold.record is already exactly the RuleRecord the d01 scaffolder would have produced standalone, so the fold-in is additive, not a breaking rename.

statement: Workspace-wide clippy::expect_used=deny (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints.clippy]) applies to test code under --all-targets too, not just library code. Two `.expect("...")` calls on `Option<T>` in feedback.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module and in tests/feedback.rs failed `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` even though the surrounding crate's src-only expect (on a provably-infallible Sha256 parse) was fine under a scoped #[allow(clippy::expect_used)].
why: Easy to assume test code is exempt from workspace lint denies since so many crates' tests read comfortably with expect()-style assertions; it is not exempt here, and clippy --all-targets checks it.
howToApply: In any test in this workspace, replace `option.expect("msg")` with a `let Some(x) = option else { return Err("msg".into()); };` pattern (tests here return Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>) instead of reaching for expect/unwrap, even in obviously-should-always-succeed test assertions. For a src-side conversion that is genuinely infallible given an upstream contract (e.g. parsing a value produced by a function whose own contract guarantees the shape), use the established narrowly-scoped `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` on a small dedicated function (precedent: enforcer_mechanization::parity::diagnostic_relpath) rather than threading a fallible Result through every caller.

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-mechanization --all-targets -- -D warnings: 2 'used expect() on a Result/Option value' errors before fix, in src/feedback.rs test mod and tests/feedback.rs
